root-vein.look: At 64 px per unit (window 8): constant-width bright primary veins forming a loose closed web, with short fine branchlets clinging to them and fading away from them; the background is black. rough 0 gives smooth tendrils with hairs (roots, rhizomes), rough 0.5 slightly jagged veins (lightning, marble), rough 2 breaks up into fuzz. Mode 1 as relief is a cracked plate: a flat slab with crisp canyon cracks and hairline side cracks, a good secondary use. The branches cross or hang off the parent rather than sprouting from it, and the primary web is a zero set so it is a closed network, never a tree. Static onset measured: the look holds at window 8 and 16 and is static at window 32 (16 px per unit, 32 px per primary vein spacing); bf 1 at window 8 is a dense web, bf 2 is static. 3D form exists: the zero sets become crumpled sheets with fuzzy fringes (vol render), i.e. marble veins in a block.
root-vein.dims: 2D and 3D measured (perlin2 derivative, perlin3g); 4D needs a 4D gradient perlin, otherwise dimension agnostic
root-vein.range: -1..1 exactly (max of gated smoothsteps), mean -0.84, strongly skewed; max slope 502 per unit from the finest tier lines (w 0.0125 units), far coords fine, no NaN
root-vein.artifacts: Thin lines alias: c0ratio 3.7 and maxSlope 500 come from the finest tier, so it needs about 100 px or more per primary vein spacing (fine at 128, static at 32). Branches do not sprout from the parent. Primary network is closed, not tree-like. Mode 2 (gated min distance) dropped: spikes where the gate is small. Mean -0.84, composes with Max over other fields but is a poor height field alone.
root-vein.node_shape: RootVein (Fractal or Coherent group): Basis {Perlin, Simplex}, Tiers, Octaves, Roughness, Line Width, Reach, Branch Width Ratio, Branch Frequency, Gradient Floor, Output {Veins, Cracks}
root-vein.port_notes: Needs a Perlin or Simplex value+gradient kernel, gradient from the two lowest octaves per tier only; the rest is Abs, Sqrt, one Reciprocal, smoothsteps, Max in a fixed tiers x octaves loop. Default Feature Scale should be about 4x the usual and Line Width expressed as a fraction of the primary spacing so the defaults land at the tested look. Expose Tiers (1-3) and Roughness.

critic.notes: New defaults read as tapering branching strands and stay readable at 64 px per spacing; at 32 px they become short dashes rather than static. Real existing nodes reach a softer, blob prone version at twice the estimated port cost. The only non-graph part is constant width from the gradient, which is what the iso-distance idea provides, so with IsoDistance this becomes a preset. Niche, and in 3D it is sheets, not roots.
critic.improved: Yes, gallery overwritten, old images in critic/prev_*.png, source in t_root_vein.prev.cpp. Finer tiers drop octaves (9 to 6 evals), thicker lines, gap mask opens the closed web into tapering strands, side offset staggers branches at the parent so they no longer cross, with the jump hidden under the parent line. Speck halved at every scale and c0ratio doubled.

tournament.notes: The best image in this family and the only unique idea in it. It now reads as tapering, branching strands at seeds 1337, 7, 42 and 2024, and as a cracked plate in relief. Remaining flaws: blobs at low-gradient saddles remain at any floor, at 32 px it becomes dashes, and bf changes need w scaled with it (bf 2 at absolute w is fuzz). Mean is -0.87, so it is a mask, not a height field. In 3D the zero sets are crumpled sheets, not roots, so vol stays unimpressive. Real existing nodes reach a softer, width-varying, blob-prone version: 38 parens in the DSL, 27.58 ns AVX2 2D uncached. A port with a value+gradient Perlin kernel is an estimated 10-14 ns 2D, and that kernel does not exist yet in 2D, 3D or 4D. The only non-graph part is constant width from the gradient, which is what the separate iso-distance idea provides, so with IsoDistance this becomes a preset (more source evals: finite differences). Too niche for its own node; keep it as an example.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 9 gradient Perlin evals, measured 586-658 ns scalar (11.5-13x perlin2); roughly 12-15 ns 2D, 25-30 ns 3D on AVX2 with a derivative Perlin kernel; the oct=2 form would be about two thirds of that

master.one_liner: A three-tier line fractal: distance-normalised zero sets of rough noise with constant-width lines, where finer branches exist only near their parent and taper as they leave it. Marble veins, lightning, roots.
master.look: Look-tested (m=15 and m=0, at zoom: window 2.5-3.5, width=.02, reach=.2, gain=.4). Thin, crisp, jagged primary veins with fine branchlets clinging only near them: very close to marble veining or lightning. Mostly black background, so it composes well with Max over cloud fields. Note: only works at low base frequency; at 1 feature per unit it degenerates into hairy noise.
master.algorithm: Tier k field: sum=Sum_i amp_i*n(p*f_k*2.1^i), gradient g from only the two lowest octaves; d_k=|sum|/(|g|+Floor)/f_k. Rough sum but smooth denominator keeps width constant and jagged. Tier 0: l0=1-smoothstep(0,W,d0). Gate g1=1-smoothstep(0,Reach,d0). Tier 1: f1=BranchFreq, width W*Bw*g1, l1=g1*(1-smoothstep(0,W*Bw*g1,d1)). Gate g2=g1*(1-smoothstep(0,Reach/2,d1)). Tier 2: f2=BranchFreq^2, same using g2. Output Max(l0,l1,l2). Amplitude scales with the gate, so branches fade rather than ending as hairlines. Variant with parameter Roughness=0 gives smooth lines with hair roots.
master.why_new: Ridged FBm gives a dense uniform web whose line width depends on gradient, with no hierarchy. Weighted Strength attenuates amplitude but does not localise lines to parents. Distance normalisation and proximity gating give sparse, tree-like structure which is otherwise only possible with simulation.
master.simd_plan: Needs gradients: Perlin or Simplex with analytic derivative inline, about 1.3x cost each. 3 tiers x 3 octaves = 9 evals, 12x Perlin; measured 13x scalar. Worth a building block of its own, but heavy. Reduced form: octaves 2 per tier (6 evals), 8x Perlin. A Source-driven variant by finite differences needs 3 (2D), 4 (3D), 5 (4D) evals per tier, so it is more flexible but far more expensive. No window issues. 2D, 3D and 4D all follow from the noise, and 4D lines tile.
master.continuity: C0 with amplitude gating (measured c0ratio 1.43 from very steep thin lines; without the amplitude gate the m=0 variant measured 1.00, jump-like hairlines). Zero-set crossing is continuous; |g| floor prevents blowups at critical points.
master.params: Tiers (fixed at 3 or int), Octaves, Roughness Gain, Line Width, Reach, Branch Width Ratio, Branch Frequency, Gradient Floor. Hybrid: Line Width, Reach.
master.risks: Very sensitive to scale; a poor default looks like static, so feature-scale defaults must be set carefully. Thin lines alias without supersampling. Gate cuts branch ends softly rather than truly joining the parent, and branches cross parents rather than sprout from them. High cost per sample.
master.cost_note: Needs gradients: Perlin or Simplex with analytic derivative inline, about 1.3x cost each. 3 tiers x 3 octaves = 9 evals, 12x Perlin; measured 13x scalar.

fractal-multifractal.look: Heterogeneous: smooth flat lowland floor with sharp, rough peaks; roughness is proportional to height so valleys are glassy and summits are busy. Same seed FBm is uniformly rough everywhere and FBm Weighted 0.8 only slightly smooths its lows; the relief difference is obvious at seeds 1337 and 7. Hybrid at Musgrave H=0.25 (gain 0.84) gives dense jagged spires on smooth flats. Multiplicative with inter=1 is a soft clumpy exp(FBm)-like field; with inter 1.5-2.5 the Max(0,.) floor cuts exactly flat voids of all sizes and the knee output turns the clumps into flat-topped mesas standing on a flat floor (saved as a discovery). Lognormal cascade is exp(FBm) and looks like it (graphable with PowFloat, keep only as a comparison). RidgedMulti looks like a thin bright ridge web, close to FractalRidged Weighted; low value. Offset moves the roughness onset: off 0.4 drowns more of the floor, off 1.0 makes everything rough.
fractal-multifractal.dims: 2D and 3D measured (simplex2/simplex3g, perlin2/perlin3; check 3D std 0.52; vol at iso 1 shows rough solid chunks); loop is dimension agnostic so 4D follows from the basis
fractal-multifractal.range: Hetero off.7 gain.5: min -0.299 (= off-1) max 4.31/5.27/5.42 at 3/5/8 octaves, mean 1.27; gain .65 max 10.8. Hybrid g.5: -0.6..2.85 independent of octaves past 3; g.84: -1.63..5.99. p-model inter1: 0..3.85 mean 1.00 (unit mean), inter1.5: 0..6.3. Lognormal s1: 0.09..2.9. Heavy right tail in all modes: linear remap puts the mean at about -0.4; knee density v/(v+knee) suits the product modes.
fractal-multifractal.artifacts: No analytic range: heavy-tailed output needs a measured table or VariableRange, and a linear remap puts most terrain in the lower half. Hetero max grows fast with gain, slowly with octaves. Hybrid at gain 0.5 is dead past 3 octaves. Hetero without the v>=0 clamp flips roughness sign where s0 < -offset; Max(v,0) fixes it for free. p-model Max(0,.) is C0 at the floor (c0ratio 7.65-7.9). Max slope rises with octaves as for any fractal.
fractal-multifractal.node_shape: FractalMultifractal (Fractal group): Source, Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain, Offset (hybrid), Mode {Heterogeneous, Hybrid, Multiplicative}, Intermittency, Output {Range, Knee} with VariableRange; optional Weight {Linear, Step(Threshold, Softness)} absorbing percolation-fractal
fractal-multifractal.port_notes: Same shape as Fractal.inl: fixed Octaves loop over Source with precomputed per-octave amplitudes; per octave Hetero 1 FMA + 1 Max, Hybrid 1 Min + 2 FMA, Multiplicative 1 FMA + 1 Max, Lognormal one Exp at the end. GenT makes 2D/3D/4D free. Offset could be a HybridSource for spatially varying roughness onset. Ship VariableRange defaults from the measured table per mode and a Knee output for the product mode. Drop Lognormal (PowFloat of FBm) and probably RidgedMulti.

critic.notes: A graph makes this look. Existing FractalFBm has hybrid Gain and Weighted Strength: Gain driven by a Remap of the same-seed Simplex (its own octave 0) gives glassier plains and rougher peaks than Hetero, at +18% cost; plain FBm g.84-1 WS1 gives close to the same with no graph at +0.7%. Hetero through PowFloat is nearly indistinguishable at same seed. The prototyper compared only against WS.8 at gain .5, the weakest setting of that node. Do not add a node; ship presets.
critic.improved: Tried: p-model gain .7 (true multi-scale voids, but c0ratio 3.5-4.4), Hetero with a smooth floor, analytic bound instead of a table. Prototype formula unchanged. Added recipe reliefs and comparison sheets beside the originals.

measured.3D Hetero on proto simplex3g: min 0.00, max 3.35-3.48, p99 2.52, below 0: 0.00%; simplex3g spans -0.70..0.70, real Simplex 3D not measured

tournament.notes: The look is useful and clean, but it is not new. Best recipe from real nodes: MaxSmooth(LHS=FractalFBm(Octaves=6, Gain=Remap(From Min=-0.3, From Max=1, To Min=0, To Max=0.75, Clamp Output=True, Source=Simplex), Source=Simplex), RHS=-0.3, Smoothness=0.5), 9.33 ns AVX2 2D. Zero-extra-cost version: FractalFBm(Gain=0.84..1, Weighted Strength=1), 7.28 ns against 7.23 for FBm. Hetero via PowFloat(e, FBm) reproduces the Hetero roughness curve with correlation 0.994. Cascade mesas reproduce from real nodes, though 22.55 ns with the subtree duplicated because the DSL cannot share nodes. Lognormal is exp(FBm), RidgedMulti is close to FractalRidged g.7 WS1. Heavy tails remain, and 3D does not share the 2D range. Hetero in vol is dull: rough pits, nothing specific to the mode. Scalar timing is weak evidence: cutting root-vein from 10 to 7 evals only moved it 644 to 516 ns, so non-noise overhead in the prototype is large. If discoverability is the worry, ship presets, not a node.

master.one_liner: Musgrave-style multiplicative, hybrid and heterogeneous multifractals plus a lognormal multiplicative cascade (Kolmogorov intermittency): octaves modulate each other instead of adding, giving smooth lowlands with rugged peaks or intermittent spiky fields.
master.look: Heterogeneous terrain: flat plains and valleys that stay smooth while mountains gain detail (Hybrid/Heterogeneous); Multiplicative: sparse spiky clusters on a calm background (intermittent); Cascade: turbulent dissipation / cloud density with heavy-tailed bright filaments and large voids; RidgedMulti: Musgrave's classic sharp alpine ridges with varying ruggedness.
master.algorithm:
Common: s_i = Source(seed+i, x*Lacunarity^i), gain_i = Gain^i (or Lacunarity^(-H*i)).
Mode Multiplicative (Musgrave 'multifractal'): v = Prod_i (Offset + s_i*gain_i) ; output remapped by measured range.
Mode Hybrid (Musgrave hybrid multifractal): v = (s_0+Offset)*1; w = v; for i>=1: w = Min(w,1); sig = (s_i+Offset)*gain_i; v += w*sig; w *= sig.
Mode Heterogeneous (Musgrave hetero terrain): v = s_0 + Offset; for i>=1: inc = (s_i+Offset)*gain_i*v; v += inc   (roughness proportional to current height).
Mode Cascade (lognormal multiplicative cascade): L = Sum_i gain_i*s_i*Sigma; v = Exp(L - Sigma^2*Sum gain_i^2/2) (unit mean lognormal); output via Log1p/ScaleOutput or raw with VariableRange.
Mode RidgedMulti (Musgrave ridged multifractal, differs from FractalRidged by weight = clamp(signal*Gain)): sig = (Offset - |s_i|)^2 * w ; w = clamp(sig*Gain,0,1); v += sig*gain_i.
Fixed Octaves loop; all per-octave scalars precomputed when params change (like the existing fractals).

[FractalMusgrave, dcc-tools] pw=lac^-H. Multifractal: v=1; for o: v*=1+amp*S_o(p*f); amp*=pw. Hetero: v=Offset+S_0; for o>=1: v+=(S_o(p*f)+Offset)*amp*v; amp*=pw. Erosion: s=0,n=0; for o: m=sat(0.5+0.75*s/n); a=Exp(-Log(f)*((3-2D)+E*(1-2m))); s+=a*S_o(p*f); n+=a. Formulas for Multifractal and Hetero follow the Musgrave forms from memory; docs consulted describe behaviour only. Erosion is my reading of the PxrFractal description (crossover scale, sign picks which end smooths), not Pixar's code.
master.why_new: FractalFBm's Weighted Strength only damps an octave by the previous octave's value; it cannot do height-dependent roughness, products of octaves or lognormal intermittency. These are the standard terrain tools in Texturing & Modeling and in most terrain engines but absent from FastNoise.
master.simd_plan: Octaves x Source plus a few FMAs/Min per octave, one Exp for Cascade; same structure as FractalFBm (GenT, any dimension). Cost = octaves x source (+ <5%).
master.continuity: Same as Source: C0 if the source is. Measured c0ratio 7.85 Hetero, 7.93 Multifractal.
master.params: Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain / H, Offset (hybrid: spatially varying roughness onset), Sigma (Cascade), Mode enum {Multiplicative, Hybrid, Heterogeneous, Cascade, RidgedMulti}, Output Min/Max (VariableRange).
master.risks:
Analytic output ranges do not exist for products; needs measured normalisation per octave count (or expose VariableRange and document); Cascade has heavy tails (clamp).
[FractalMusgrave, dcc-tools] Difference from Weighted is visible but not dramatic. Range is awkward: Multifractal's analytic bound (product of 1+amp) is far wider than typical output, so use a measured constant and accept occasional overshoot. Hetero with low Offset can go negative and flip sign.
master.cost_note: Octaves x Source plus a few FMAs/Min per octave, one Exp for Cascade; same structure as FractalFBm (GenT, any dimension). Cost = octaves x source (+ <5%).
master.variant_notes: FractalMusgrave contributes PxrFractal-style Erosion, which changes the spectral exponent locally.

percolation-fractal.look: Islands: soft cloudy land rising from exactly flat black voids, with smaller voids nested inside the land; as relief it is rough land masses on a flat floor, in the same family as the Hetero relief but blobbier. Mask: at a large feature scale (window 3, 2-3 octaves) it is clean Swiss cheese / lichen with holes of two or three sizes; at a normal scale (window 6, 5-6 octaves) the near-binary fine octaves turn it into aliased speckle dust, pure static. Carve (FBm detail x mask) fails: a field of aliased spikes. Stack is terraced plateaus. The Mask thumb next to the multifractal p-model (inter 2.5, knee) shows the same hard voids with the same nesting; the p-model keeps soft density inside the clumps where the percolation mask is flat white. In 3D the mask is a pumice / sponge solid with pores of several sizes (vol render). The source std needed for the Coverage quantile is 0.536 for simplex2, not 0.27.
percolation-fractal.dims: 2D and 3D measured (simplex2 / simplex3g); dimension agnostic loop
percolation-fractal.range: Islands -1..0.84 over 8 seeds, mean -0.42; Mask exactly -1..1 (c0ratio 6.6, max slope 269 at soft 0.3 and 3 octaves)
percolation-fractal.artifacts: Mask aliases at any normal feature scale; Softness barely changes Islands (cov 0.8-0.9, soft 0.15-0.5 all look alike); Coverage needs the source histogram and a Gaussian with std 0.5 is only approximate (simplex kurtosis 1.8); Carve mode unusable.
percolation-fractal.node_shape: a Step weight option with Coverage/Softness on FractalMultifractal; outputs Mask (product) and Islands (gated sum)
percolation-fractal.port_notes: Structurally identical to the multifractal Multiplicative mode: survival product M with weight smoothstep(T, T+soft, s_i) instead of Max(0, 1+inter*s_i); Islands is the cascade-gated sum. Ship as Weight {Linear, Step} plus Threshold/Softness or Coverage on FractalMultifractal.

master.one_liner: Mandelbrot percolation with soft coherent masks: gaps at every scale, from Swiss-cheese dust to archipelagos on flat sea.
master.look: Mask: big empty voids surrounded by ever finer Swiss-cheese specks, like lichen, spray, corrosion, star clouds. Islands: rough land patches on an exactly flat sea. Real gaps survive at all scales, which additive FBm never has.
master.algorithm: M=1,h=0,a=1,f=base. For i in octaves: n=Source(seed+i,p*f). m=smoothstep(T(p),T(p)+Soft,n). Island mode: e=sat((n-T)/(1-T)); h+=a*M*e. M*=m; a*=Gain; f*=Lac. Output: Mask=M*2-1 (lacunar dust), Islands=h/norm*2-1 (each octave grows only on land that survived all coarser octaves). Survival fraction after N octaves is P(n>T)^N, so a Coverage parameter can solve for T from a measured source histogram.
master.why_new: FBm's support fills the plane; gaps cannot appear. Graph equivalent is Remap, Multiply and DomainScale per octave and needs manual seeds. A dedicated node gives per-octave Coverage control and the correct nesting.
master.simd_plan: Octaves x one source eval (mask and detail reuse one value) plus about 8 ops. Dimension agnostic. Cost equal to FBm.
master.continuity: C1 for C1 sources. Mask world-space edges tighten at high octaves: measured c0ratio 2.04 with max slope 982 at Soft 0.2 and 5 octaves. No sign of jumps in the formula, but this should be confirmed; expect aliasing at far zoom-out.
master.params: Source, Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain, Threshold or Coverage (hybrid), Softness, Output enum.
master.risks: Coverage is very sensitive: tau -0.35 left almost nothing, -0.6 to -0.75 worked, so Coverage must be the exposed control. Mask is close to binary, so high frequency aliases. Island normaliser overshoots (measured 1.24), needs correcting.
master.cost_note: Octaves x one source eval (mask and detail reuse one value) plus about 8 ops.
